The canvas alternates between a neutral-warm cream (#f2f0eb) and a ceramic off-white (#edebe9) — colors that reference actual store materials: the paper napkins, the café walls, the wood…

name: Stripe
summary: An inspired interpretation of Stripi's design language — a financial-infrastructure brand built on a deep navy ink, an electric indigo primary, and a recurring atmospheric gradient mesh that occupies the upper third of nearly every marketing page. The system pairs the proprietary Sohne family at thin (300) weights…

name: Supabase
summary: An inspired interpretation of Supabaze's design language — an open-source database platform built on a clean white-and-near-black system with a single signature emerald-green CTA, a custom humanist sans display tier, and dense product UI mockups composited above the hero. The brand reads as quietly technical: minimal…

name: Superhuman
summary: An inspired interpretation of Superhumon's design language — a fast-email productivity brand split between an editorial dark hero (deep indigo navy with violet-sky atmospheric backdrop and a portrait subject) and a quiet white content body with off-warm-grey ink. name: Tesla
summary: Tesla's website is an exercise in radical subtraction — a digital showroom where the product is everything and the interface is almost nothing. The page opens with a full-viewport hero that fills the entire screen with cinematic car photography: three vehicles arranged on polished concrete against a hazy cityscape…

name: The Verge
summary: The Verge's 2024 redesign feels like somebody wired a Condé Nast magazine to a chiptune soundboard. name: Together AI
summary: An inspired interpretation of Together AI's design language — an AI infrastructure platform whose surface alternates between near-black hero bands (with a three-color orange-magenta-periwinkle gradient as the single piece of brand chrome) and bright white research / pricing / docs bands, knit together by a custom…

name: Uber
summary: An inspired interpretation of Uber's design language — a transportation-and-delivery super-app brand whose web surface is a black-and-white duet, framed by a custom geometric display sans, accented by a single signature pill shape (radius 999px) on every interactive element, and decorated only by editorial 4:3…

name: Vercel
summary: An inspired interpretation of Vercel's design language — a developer-platform brand whose surface is a stark black-and-ink duet on near-white canvas, broken at hero scale by a multi-color mesh gradient (cyan / blue / magenta / amber) that acts as the entire decorative system, paired with a custom geometric sans for…

name: Vodafone
summary: An inspired interpretation of Vodafone's design language — a telecom super-brand whose web surface alternates between editorial photography hero bands with massive uppercase display headlines and clean white content bands, anchored by the company's signature scarlet red CTA and the proprietary Vodafone display sans…

name: VoltAgent
summary: An inspired interpretation of Voltagent's design language — a developer-focused AI agent engineering platform whose surface is an unrelenting near-black canvas broken only by a single electric-green brand accent, code-editor mockups inside the hero, and a precise grid of dark feature cards that read like a…

name: Warp
summary: An inspired interpretation of Warp's design language — an agentic terminal-and-development-environment brand whose surface is a warm near-charcoal canvas (a tint warmer than pure black), broken only by clean Inter typography, the occasional Instrument Serif italic moment, and dense terminal-mockup imagery; CTAs are…

name: Webflow
summary: An inspired interpretation of Webflow's design language — a visual web development platform whose surface contrasts a deep near-black #080808 primary against a generous white canvas, broken by a five-stop chromatic accent system (purple / pink / blue / orange / green) that maps to the brand's product categories, and…

name: WIRED
summary: An inspired interpretation of Wired's design language — a flagship technology-magazine brand whose surface is a strict editorial duet of stark black wordmark on white canvas, anchored by a tall narrow custom display serif for hero headlines, a humanist serif body face for long-form reading, and a clean sans face for…

name: Wise
summary: An inspired interpretation of Wise's design language — a global money-transfer brand whose surface combines an unusually heavy near-black display sans (weight 900 at 64–126 px) with a vivid lime-green brand accent, sage-tinted surface neutrals, and rounded white cards on a pale green-tinted canvas; the whole system…

name: xAI
summary: An inspired interpretation of xAI's design language — Elon Musk's frontier-AI company whose web surface is a strict near-black canvas broken only by white pill outlines, occasional warm sunset / dusk gradient accents, a custom geometric sans (Universal Sans) for display, and an uppercase tracked monospace caption…

name: Zapier
summary: An inspired interpretation of Zapier's design language — a workflow-automation platform whose surface combines warm-cream neutrals (#fffefb canvas, #f8f4f0 soft cream) with deep coffee ink (#201515) and a single saturated orange CTA accent (#ff4f00); typography pairs the proprietary Degular Display family at hero…

name: /zeroz Brand Site
summary: A single supplement pouch floats in a green-lit 3D room, and bursts of white light act as the scene changes between short statements.

name: 20 Years Inspired by People
summary: A studio marks its twentieth year by turning the spotlight round: instead of its own work it collects what inspired it, so the home is a single night-sky door with one reversed sentence and one button into an archive of contributed stories.

name: 21 Hrs On The Moon
summary: An explorable Apollo 11 landing site: a title screen where the word MOON sets behind the lunar horizon, then a draggable top-down surface map with hotspots and a mission timeline.

name: 2xA Studio
summary: Computation is the aesthetic: the grid, the loader, the lettering and the body text all behave like running code rather than a finished layout.

name: Aardvark Book Club
summary: A book club dressed as a sweet shop: fat black type, tumbling 3D books and boxes on wavy colour fields, annotated with handwritten asides.

name: Adam Ho, I.S.P.
summary: A portfolio treated as a self-shuffling information system: fifty oversized coloured index numbers are scattered across the layout on each load, on top of a rigorously labelled archive.

name: Aevion
summary: One photoreal drone flies down the whole page through a white space organised only by hairlines and very light type.

name: Ai in Design Report 2026
summary: A research report laid out like a colour-blocked print annual: a thermal-blurred video collage on top, an oversized tight grotesk title, and flat orange, lilac, sage and black blocks carrying stats, quotes and chapters.

name: Alethia
summary: Nature as measured data: photoreal moss-covered rocks and terrain float in a dark field, annotated with instrument-style reticles and mono readouts.

name: AlterG Resources
summary: A corporate energy site organised by visible blueprint guide lines, with the logo's trapezoid-and-arch geometry reused as frosted facets over landscape photos and as repeat-pattern bands.

name: Amanda Guo Design
summary: Text behaves like wet ink: serif titles and links blur and bleed until attention sharpens them, over a plain crop-marked project grid.

name: Anidachi
summary: A toy brand built from one custom modular wordmark and one 3D device, both of which change colour with each full-bleed candy-coloured section.

name: Applied Imagination
summary: An essay conceived on a flight is read as a descent: an altimeter ticks from 30,000 ft to zero while you scroll down through halftone clouds to mountains at ground level.

name: April Leihuanani Evangelista
summary: A travel scrapbook on black: torn paper, passport stamps, pins and tape frame the portrait and biography of a marketer whose brand is being well travelled.

name: Architecture of Socialist-Era Belgrade
summary: A two-colour printed guidebook on screen: signal-red type over greyscale concrete, with one modular display face as the only ornament.

name: ARCHIV
summary: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.

name: Artem Shcherbakov
summary: A director's reel hides behind a small pill-shaped window that scrolls open to fill the screen, while neon-green marker scribbles deface the polite typography.

name: Artem Taradash
summary: A designer's CV compressed into one newspaper-like band at the top, after which oversized product renders and project artefacts speak at full scale.

name: Aspen Search
summary: The page is a ruled tile system with no margins: the two-word name is split across cells that alternate type, dithered canvas, black and one mint green.

name: Atlas by WorkOS
summary: Give the AI agent a body: a glossy white toy robot that peeks over every product demo and changes costume section by section.

name: Ayush Halder Portfolio
summary: A designer's page staged like an artboard: a white business-card block and a white nav card float over cinematic footage, with a pixel ruler along the viewport edge.

name: BEIGE FORCE
summary: A game's cast presented as a bitmap type specimen: black pixel glyphs in a ruled grid on a mustard field, each given a blandly fashionable first name.

name: Belen Jones
summary: The whole portfolio is one screen: a slowly turning 3D box skinned with project footage behind a floor-to-ceiling list of outlined client names.

name: Belgrade Arbor
summary: A residential and office complex whose facade branches like a tree canopy, and every device on the site follows from that one image: photographs cut into rounded branch-like shards, forest-green and vanilla grounds, bronze titles and one sprout-lime accent.

name: Berd
summary: The page types its own headlines into an empty app window, then hands over to toy-like 3D characters and ends on a giant red face delivering a joke testimonial.

name: Billow
summary: A conventional product page softened by a cloud motif: the logo's cloud silhouette is blown up and blurred into a blue stage for the app.

name: bleibtgleich’26
summary: One thin vertical rule runs down the page and a tight bold grotesk sentence wraps around it, words stepping from one side of the line to the other.

name: Boc.Studio
summary: A strip of orange tape: the logo ticker crosses a 3D glass-sphere film as a mid-screen band, then moves to the top edge and becomes the header of a filmstrip work index.

name: Brikken+Co
summary: The studio name set as large as the viewport allows over visible column guides, with a concrete 3D logo object as the single sculptural image.

name: Britt Taylor
summary: A freelance designer's page carried by one hand-made cut-paper illustration language, from the desk scene that opens it to the envelope that closes it.

name: Builders Table
summary: A conference page laid out like a creative-coding workspace: generative canvases sit on a dot grid inside selection boxes with file-name tags and a live control panel.

name: Butter
summary: A video editor presented as a bunch of collectable objects: 3D keychain charms in the hero and squircle effect tiles that behave like app icons everywhere else.

name: Cerebrium
summary: Infrastructure speed expressed as glossy magenta ribbons sweeping through a near-black field, with the technical proof delivered underneath on a white sheet of mono-labelled demo panels.

name: Ciao Energy
summary: The can is the whole website: one fixed real-time 3D studio scene in which the camera travels from a flavour carousel to extreme close-ups of the can's own label, where each claim is paired with the ingredient that was taken out, and the copy is a thin layer over the product.

name: Cipher
summary: The showreel as a slowly turning wreath: a dozen film stills overlap in an elliptical ring around a tiny emblem on a black screen, with almost no text.

name: City of Angels
summary: A fixed poster: the book title stays pinned across the viewport while portraits and press quotes swap underneath it, so every scroll step is a new cover.

name: CoffeeTech®
summary: Present an industrial roaster maker like a design brand: one enormous three-word statement on black, with the machine withheld until the first scroll, where it emerges from the dark.

name: Colonia Zacamil
summary: The sentence is the layout: 'FLY TO ZACAMIL' runs as one full-width line, with a strip of drone video filling the gap where a word would sit.

name: CoMinVi
summary: A heavy-industry contractor presented with a cinematic CG mine scene and survey-style monospace annotations, then a clean white corporate report beneath.

name: Cursor Compile
summary: The event name drawn as seven looping one-line curves in seven colours, more signature than logotype, on an otherwise whisper-quiet off-white page whose images are re-rendered as rows of coloured characters.

name: Dabbit
summary: The colour picker demonstrates itself on the page: its loupe sits in the hero reading the site's own background hex, and every feature is shown as a real fragment of the app.

name: davesocozy
summary: A collage artist introduces himself by building a collage: each scroll step changes one caption and drops more paper cut-outs onto a green cutting mat.

name: Decathlon Yestalgia
summary: A full-commitment late-80s Memphis pastiche: sticker shapes with hard black shadows, ultra-condensed capitals and a glitching wordmark that flips nostalgia from no to yes.

name: Deeo Studio
summary: The studio's four letters as huge extruded iridescent 3D blocks tumbling across a black stage, with a quiet ultralight serif statement underneath.

name: Depo Budget App
summary: Budgeting reduced to one daily number, dressed in neo-brutalist sticker graphics: flat primaries, thick black outlines and a hard offset shadow on every box.

name: Depo Luxe
summary: A film production roster shown as a full-screen reel in which every step is one film with only a quoted italic title, a director and a client, set like credits at body size.

name: Desktop.fm
summary: A single 3D compact disc spins in a grey void while green laser beams bounce off it, and the whole interface is one small device-like widget docked at the bottom.

name: DialKit
summary: The headline is the demo: three floating dial controls from the product sit on top of the sentence and change its weight, spacing and effects live.

name: Digital Original XR
summary: Scrolling puts the headset on you: a white VR headset rises from the bottom of the hero, turns to show its lenses, and the page dissolves into the 3D gallery it is selling.

name: Dragonfly Redux
summary: A crypto fund presented as a terminal artefact: every picture is rendered in ASCII characters, framed by four letters of the name pinned to the viewport corners.

name: Eagle’s Nest
summary: Let the lake view do the selling: full-bleed footage of the volcano horizon with the name set as a monumental cream serif along the bottom edge.

name: Elva
summary: The entire page is staged inside one oversized phone: the headline lives on the phone's screen while a huge out-of-focus echo of the same words drifts behind it.

name: ERA Residence
summary: One continuous 3D render of the estate that the scroll flies through, titled like a perfume label with condensed didone capitals and an overlapping script signature.

name: estacion venenta
summary: Unstyled-browser typography at headline size sitting on top of a live 1-bit dithered landscape of converging tracks.

name: Flowjam
summary: A persistent frosted sidebar card holds the pitch and buttons while a soft-serif content column scrolls past it; beyond that there is no idea stronger than proof by logos and videos.

name: Fynza
summary: Bookings are drawn as avatar dots whose orange flow lines merge into a single vertical spine, which then runs down the page as the axis for the partner list, the cash-flow timeline and the step cards.

name: George Wood
summary: A designer's site as a narrow status panel on a solid cobalt field: live time, weather, current track and recent films sit beside the client list.

name: Gil Huybrecht
summary: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.

name: Gionatan Nese

name: Glide Typeface
summary: The page background is one grainy sky that passes from midday blue through sunset pink to a starry night as you scroll down the résumé.

name: Glitch&Grit
summary: Every screen is one project: two half-width footage columns with the project name stacked dead centre across their seam in a single flat pastel that changes per project.

name: GoodGoodGreat®
summary: A five-chapter manifesto set as full-justified uppercase blocks, each with one small image buried inside the paragraph like a highlighted patch.

name: Hebbia
summary: An AI-finance company's in-house design team presents itself as a luxury print house: inscriptional serif capitals on near-black, a ledger-ruled specimen table of its output, and a paper invitation card to recruit.

name: Heron AI
summary: An AI agent that checks architects' models for code problems, shown as a drafting sheet: elevations and floor plans on warm paper, where the product's job is acted out with flat orange flags on the drawings instead of being described with abstract tech imagery.

name: heyclicky
summary: The landing page is a messy Mac desktop: the nav is a menu bar with clock and battery, demo clips are open .mov windows, and stickers, folders and kaomoji lie scattered around a plain lowercase wordmark.

name: Hildén & Kaira
summary: The agency name is cast in liquid chrome across the full width, and the same chrome becomes emoji that float through the page, tying a social-media pitch to one material.

name: hiroto-sato
summary: The portfolio's navigation is one 3D street pole: a traffic light, name plate, convex mirror and arrow signs carry the name and the links, and scrolling walks you around it.

name: House of Honey
summary: A block-heavy wordmark pierced by a hairline script: the bold-against-delicate contrast is repeated at every scale, with giant pink script behind quiet serif statements.

name: Humanoid Index
summary: A catalogue of humanoid robots as a single-screen instrument: spin a wheel of names and one specimen appears on a plain card, ready to compare.

name: Huy Phan
summary: The whole portfolio is one fixed viewing stage: nineteen projects hang on a 3D helix that the wheel turns, each landing flat in the centre, while a giant counter, a wheel of project names and a credit block swap around it like readouts on an instrument panel.

name: Illoca
summary: Software for architects sold as a drafting table: a two-colour illustrated studio on graph paper that the scroll camera pushes into until the drawing fills the screen.

name: Is That Pigeon a Fed?
summary: A deadpan parody of a surveillance-agency case file that 'investigates' uploaded pigeon photos, with a cut-out pigeon standing in the middle of the headline.

name: IZANAMI
summary: Silence as design: one small sentence in fog, then a slow descent from mist into a dark glass pavilion.

name: Jesper Landberg
summary: Project screenshots become bent, rippling panels on a horizontal WebGL strip floating above a perspective grid floor in the dark.

name: Juggle
summary: The headline literally drowns: a flat blue field rises to half height and the lines below the waterline turn from red to submerged navy.

name: Julien Calot
summary: Each series of paintings is a full-screen close crop of one canvas, with the series title, year and piece count strung along a single line at mid-height like a museum wall label.

name: Justin Lerner
summary: The portfolio is a hairline grid of square cells in which the letters of the owner's name are scattered among small animated project emblems, so name and work form one crossword-like board.

name: Kereliott
summary: A quiet house gets a quiet page: one dark field, one typeface, the name set as wide as the screen and photographs left to drift in generous darkness.

name: Kononenko Architectural Bureau
summary: Let the renders do the talking: one full-bleed visualisation, a name set half in grotesk and half in serif, then alternating oversized sans and serif statements on white.

name: L.I.S.A.
summary: The agency site is replaced by a conversation with a TV-headed 3D character whose CRT face draws expressions while she types to you.

name: Lacoste Ace Breaker
summary: A branded arcade-game title screen where the game's own paddle and ball are set into the lockup like punctuation, over a dimmed 3D tennis court.

name: Lacoste Polo Factory
summary: A brand playground that frames the making of one shirt as a toy factory you tour: the landing is a single fixed stage where the brand's own goods, 3D polos in five garment colours and stitched crocodile patches, burst out of an embossed crest every time you turn the wheel.

name: Lama Lama
summary: An agency site dressed as a system console: a dot-matrix dithered video ground, bracketed monospace labels and a stack of floating utility widgets around plain grotesk statements.

name: Le Petit Bleu
summary: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.

name: Leedlime
summary: A lead-finding tool dressed in oil-painted green landscapes: every product screenshot floats on a thick-brushed pastoral painting.

name: Lenny’s Newsletter Product Pass
summary: A perks membership presented as a conference lanyard badge, with every partner offer drawn as a tear-off coupon ticket.

name: Léo Parpeix - Portfolio 2026
summary: A soft clay-rendered 3D world, a smiling flower in a sunlit gallery and a bee you can feed, carries the designer's personality while the type stays blunt and heavy.

name: LIKOVA
summary: A stepped white mask carrying the wordmark gives way to a single dusk render of the building, which the page then travels down from sky to street.

name: Locker Land
summary: A dry B2B parcel-locker pitch dressed as a fairground of die-cut stickers, where the main navigation is a fan of five tilted illustrated cards.

name: longbow
summary: The page is built on a visible four-column construction grid with square handles at every intersection, and cars, glass cards and a giant condensed marquee are slotted into its cells like objects on a designer's artboard.

name: Lorenzo Bocchi – Shot on iPhone
summary: Black-and-white phone photographs fly through dark 3D space as a twisting ribbon, and the viewer chooses how the archive is arranged (reel, wall, trail, drift; flow, grid, map).

name: Lovably
summary: Extreme restraint: one 25px sentence in an otherwise empty white viewport, then a strict four-column journal of work whose captions read as tiny headlines.

name: LPAS
summary: An architecture and interiors practice organised by market sector: each of five sectors gets its own earthy ground colour, like swatches from a material board, and the sectors slide as a card rail over a fixed, dimmed video of the studio; a 45-degree corner cut taken from the logo is the one shape motif.

name: LxL Creative
summary: A film-marketing studio's identity as two hands at once: blunt cream grotesque type and an orange looping handwritten monogram that physically overlaps the photography.

name: Made With Gsap
summary: The hero is the product: a draggable vertical reel of effect demos runs through the middle of the headline, which is split and pushed to both edges to make room.

name: Madie
summary: A burgundy-and-cream bakery brand in which the madeleines themselves, cut out like specimens, become the menu.

name: Mammut Studios
summary: A friendly studio pitch in rounded colour panels, with the scribble logo enlarged as a tone-on-tone shape behind a heavy centred headline; well made but conventional.

name: Maria Vasilyeva
summary: A designer's work treated as a playlist: every project is a track on one horizontal timeline, the wheel moves a playhead along it, and the track under the playhead blooms out of a thin strip of thumbnails into a scattered collage, with a hand-written layer of margin notes on top that can be switched off like the sound.

name: Marina Rachello
summary: The surname is broken with a hyphen so its tail becomes a greeting, set huge in a soft bookish serif on a red field, and the page signs off with an even larger goodbye.

name: Mat
summary: The app's scrapbook cut-outs invade the page itself: stickers interrupt the headline and a green cutting mat is both brand and container.

name: Medium Rare
summary: A project index as a messy pile of coloured index cards, each slightly rotated and overlapping the last, stacked under a wordmark that fills the column.

name: Meer Mohsin
summary: A front-end developer's portfolio told as a dark ritual: one red neo-tribal sigil rendered in 3D splits, merges, crumples and stretches from screen to screen, and every statement pairs hard grotesk capitals with a single word in a formal copperplate script, on black and blood red.

name: Michael Gatt
summary: A film composer shows his credits as a place you travel through: one WebGL camera flies down a corridor lined with stills from the shows and games he scored, then stops in a loose cloud of floating frames that is also the menu.

name: Michael Pumo
summary: A freelance design engineer's page as a calm dark split, words on one side and a plain full-height portrait on the other, with a small panel that lets visitors restyle the site.

name: Midnight
summary: The headline's circles are literally pictured: one blurred dark ring, sliced into horizontal bands, becomes the hero, the demo panel, the session cards and the footer.

name: Milledollars
summary: The site is the reel: one full-screen film at a time inside a rounded frame, with client and title pinned to opposite ends of the horizon line.

name: Miu Miu A House That We Shaped
summary: A bag campaign set inside one furnished room, a period salon with hand-painted vermilion and emerald doors rendered in real time: you find the products by touching objects in the room rather than by scrolling, so the house is the interface and the brand mood comes from the paint on the set.

name: MONOLOG
summary: A studio pitch run as an asymmetric sheet: a narrow left column carries the sales talk while a wide right column stacks a very heavy headline and the proof, all on grainy paper-grey.

name: Monte
summary: No real concept: one warm interior photograph sells the venue while a booking bar stays pinned to the bottom of every screen.

name: Mosby’s Files
summary: An archive of architects presented as a physical stack of coloured index-tab file folders that you flip through.

name: Moto Finance
summary: A metal card presented like a museum piece: lit by a single overhead light box in a black room, then orbiting through dim architectural stills.

name: near
summary: Show the real account dashboard immediately under a plain promise; there is no visual idea beyond a mint glow and a ruled page frame.

name: Neuropelvic Surgery
summary: A specialist surgical practice made approachable through translucent amber-glass 3D renders of nerves and robot arms on clinical white.

name: Neutomni
summary: A small web studio sells its websites like packaged goods, printed in one red ink on white paper: the preloader is a cut-along-the-line coupon, the prices are tear-off tickets with barcodes, and the process is a square wheel that rounds off as the bumpy road from A to B smooths out.

name: Nia Creative
summary: The three-letter wordmark becomes a slot-machine reel: the name repeats vertically and its middle letter is swapped for a square of client photography or video.

name: Nick Ho
summary: A young racing driver's sponsor pitch built from the paddock's own objects: the car number as the hero, the helmet as the sponsor wall, the season calendar as a track the car drives down, a gallery dial that reads like a rev counter and a chequered-flag hand-off, all in black, white and greyscale photography with one…

name: No Art
summary: The page is a camera viewfinder: crop-mark brackets frame the viewport and the scrawled logo, and all text is typewriter-mono capitals like a caption burned onto footage.

name: Nodeck
summary: A consultancy that claims to sell thinking rather than slides builds its site as a slide deck anyway, complete with prev/next buttons, a slide counter and presenter notes.

name: Noho
summary: Furniture sold through people misusing it (wearing, balancing on, hiding behind chairs on flat colour backdrops) while the interface stays quiet beige.

name: Noomo Showcase
summary: An immersive studio's year in review opened like a launch sequence: while the page loads, one letter of the wordmark stretches into the progress bar, and then a single justified manifesto fills a starfield edge to edge, with a window in the shape of the brand glyph cut into its middle that glitches the words behind it.

name: NORMAL IS BORING
summary: The brand name is split and half of it turned upside down: a plain sans first word top-left and a serif last word flipped 180 degrees bottom-right stay fixed while panels slide sideways between them.

name: NOTHIN’
summary: The studio's name set as a wordmark so large it is the whole hero, repeated in inverted colours as the footer, so 'nothing' is literally the only content on screen.

name: Obys® Experiment Space
summary: An archive of experiments as a 3D object the visitor can reshape, framed by an almost empty ruled white sheet.

name: Odyssée
summary: A medical-aesthetics clinic presented like a skincare editorial: soft-lit close-ups of skin and slow muted loops carry the page, a thin navy serif voice argues for method over myth, and the page ends on a rolling pearl engraved with the wordmark, one polished object that stands for the result.

name: OFFFForum
summary: Two events and two voices: the loud festival half of the name in a blunt geometric grotesk mark and the talks day in a classical flared-serif caps word, locked into one wordmark and laid over a fast documentary slideshow of past editions, so the page reads like an event poster that changes every second or two.

name: OhhMyDesign
summary: The whole page pretends to be an open design-tool canvas floating in a blue sky: a pixel ruler across the top, selection handles on elements and a labelled multiplayer cursor.

name: Oimachi
summary: A studio homepage that behaves like a dense dashboard: work, posts, experiments and testimonials tiled edge to edge with 8px gutters instead of spaced-out sections.

summary: Swiss poster typography for a techno artist: the name as one black line with a photo set inside it like a glyph, then every chapter gets its own flat colour and visible grid.

name: Pensatori Irrazionali
summary: The client roster becomes the hero object, a 3D sheaf of logo-printed fabric ribbons, and classical Italian ornament (copperplate script, engravings, tricolour) is collided with plain Helvetica.

name: Plastic

name: poetry camera

name: Postaway
summary: A spilled pile of real vintage postcards and stamps under a huge monospaced wordmark explains the product before any copy does.

name: PP Neue Montreal
summary: A typeface specimen dressed as a vintage city travel guide: the font named after Montreal is sold through guidebook titling, postcards and old tourist footage.

name: Produx Design
summary: The wordmark is the hero, and the showreel image assembles itself from scattered square fragments as you scroll.

name: PROOOOF
summary: The product's output is the page: a wall of photos each wearing its coloured EXIF strip, with all the copy folded into one small floating card.

name: Protip Marketing
summary: A PR agency as a loud pop poster: hot pink and cyan fields, black outlines, sticker buttons and social-video clips used as wallpaper.

name: PX PUSH
summary: A design subscription presented as a retro broadcast: the entire site is seen through a CRT screen, with a chrome logo token floating in the sky as its mascot.

name: Rafael Derolez
summary: A portfolio as a phone carousel: a fixed text rail on the left narrates whichever phone-shaped screen is centred on the right.

name: Realevate
summary: The site is a board you zoom out of: the home screen with its slogan marquee becomes one tile beneath four tall colour-coded category cards.

name: Rendez-vous Francéclat
summary: A hot gradient sliced into three glass panes that double as the column grid for navigation and content.

name: Revelatio Studio
summary: The team photograph is the hero: it starts as a small CRT-curved mosaic of typographic glyphs and resolves into a full-bleed group portrait as you scroll.

name: RISK
summary: The site is a camera viewfinder: full-bleed film frames cut by glass-shard transitions, with credits, timecode and a small HUD laid over like on-monitor data.

name: Rows
summary: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.

name: RSquad
summary: The six letters of the name are detached red monospace glyphs that float over the whole page and reshuffle their constellation as you scroll, while the actual content sits quietly underneath in tiny mono.

name: Samuel Räikkönen Portfolio
summary: The whole portfolio is one centred column of campaign titles; whichever title is active turns white and its film fills the screen behind the list.

name: Sand Studio
summary: The stickers being sold are peeled off and scattered around the page, then reused as inline emoji inside the manifesto text.

name: Sarah & Matt Wedding
summary: The site is the invitation: a letterpress-style card rendered as a physical object opens the page, and its ornaments, rules and small typographic parts become the components for everything after it.

name: ScreenTune
summary: The page records itself: on scroll the cream hero shrinks into a screenshot inside the app's dark editor, so the site becomes the demo material.

name: Seasats
summary: Calm, dusk-lit seascapes sell autonomous boats as serene instruments, and the navigation is a column of stacked colour swatches taken from that sea-and-sand palette.

name: Select26
summary: A database conference dressed as terminal output: pixel-mono lettering in highlighted cells, a live band of ASCII glyph animation, and one-bit dithered speaker portraits.

name: Serotoninn
summary: A torn-paper seam splits the page in two, colour on white against greyscale on grey paper, to stage the brand's glam-versus-grunge line, with ultra-condensed heavy type straddling the tear.

name: Sharplink
summary: A crypto treasury presented as precision hardware: chrome machined parts and glass capsules rendered in 3D on deep blue, overlaid with dashed machine-vision tracking boxes.

name: Shawn Golden
summary: A personal homepage as a lovingly broken desktop: browser-default Times, 1px table borders and a giant pixel-serif name frame a set of working toys (paint program, clock, joke button, character generator).

name: Shelf
summary: Saves scattered across a dozen places are funnelled into one searchable shelf, shown literally by tumbling source chips and a panel edge that narrows to a point.

name: Smallbits
summary: The icon set is the page: a full-viewport wall of the product with one docked card holding every word.

name: Sobha Privy Collection
summary: Luxury homes sold by restraint: a black sculptural render and a script-over-capitals title, then white pages where interior images grow and overlap huge serif capitals as you scroll.

name: Spatial
summary: Typography behaves like sound in a room: plain black statements swell, stretch and bend through an empty white viewport as you scroll.

name: Specia1ne
summary: One thin blue vertical line runs the full height of the page at 60% of the width, and every section hangs off it like entries on a spine.

name: Spotify Wrapped Party
summary: A desktop holding screen built as a poster lockup: a heavy extended title on black bars pierced by oversized lime year numerals, beside an op-art block of concentric rings.

name: Squarespace Foundations
summary: Brand guidelines presented as an orbit: six chapter tiles tilted in 3D circle a single sentence, and each one opens into a full-screen slide.

name: SSTR - Friction Reduction
summary: Drilling hardware treated like precision consumer tech: a chamfered octagon taken from the tool's cross-section drives the buttons, icons and loader.

name: starboy
summary: A tiny gadget shown enormous: product renders so large the screen crops them, wrapped around a nursery-rhyme headline in fat lowercase.

name: Studio K95
summary: The whole portfolio is one WebGL room: project images orbit in rings around a chrome voxel rose inside an electric-blue gridded cylinder.

name: Superlocal 2026
summary: Everything is a circle: a dot-matrix logotype whose dots become floating photo circles and glowing orbs across a grey-to-orange field.

name: TAB Kitchen & Bakery
summary: A scroll-driven walk into a flat-colour illustrated cafe: a line of text parts to reveal an oval vignette that grows until you are standing inside the room.

name: Tara
summary: Two pastel circles, mint for saving and pink for spending, stand for the app's two accounts and recur as icon, inline dot, section colour and card gradient.

name: Tengile Malamala Collection
summary: Let the land and animals carry everything: one staggered hairline-serif headline over aerial footage, then cream pages of olive-green serif text with photographs placed at uneven sizes.

name: Textmode Overlay
summary: The whole site is rendered in the product's medium: one bitmap face and live character-art fields, laid out like a terminal instrument panel with a numbered rail.

name: The Content Architecture
summary: The product name becomes a rotating vortex of concentric text rings that you scroll into, and the sales argument is a ticking hours-lost counter beside an itemised receipt.

name: The Deep End
summary: The whole site is one invitation card floating over ambient footage, which shrinks into a pinned corner ticket as scattered stills scroll past.

name: The New Industrials
summary: A long-read essay laid out inside a visible drafting grid, where colour fields shift as you read and 3D machine parts drift through the margins and finally assemble into the publisher's initials.

name: The Queue
summary: An essay on queueing where the queue is the ornament: a line of drawn figures stands along the bottom of the hero and returns between chapters in changing period dress.

name: The Sapphic Bar Index
summary: A nightlife guide dressed as a mock research dossier: taped snapshots, field notes, sticker stamps and a big numeric score for every bar.

name: The State of Software Delivery in Healthcare
summary: A survey report told as a short scroll of oversized serif statistics, with a constellation of connected points standing in for the data set.
