name: The state of the gallery
summary: A year-in-review told as a flight over a glowing particle landscape, where each statistic or pick is a single word floating in 3D space.

name: The Tie-break
summary: The start screen of a branded tennis game, where the lines of a court seen from above become the frame around the title; only this screen was captured.

name: The Tuscan Journey Begins
summary: A bag campaign told as a painted train journey: you enter through a ticket-shaped title card hung inside an illustrated vintage carriage, with the bag resting on a suitcase.

name: The Watch
summary: A single 3D watch is the only actor: it holds centre stage and turns, flips and finally explodes into parts while giant product-name letters slide behind and in front of it.

name: Tiny Computer Co.
summary: A software studio presented as a plain text log: one serif sentence, then monospace notes with dates in a narrow left column, and nothing else.

name: Transport
summary: Present a USB stick as a luxury object: one studio render on charcoal above a chrome custom wordmark, then let moody macro photography carry the rest.

name: Trevor Noah
summary: The comedian as a paper cut-out sticker: his head is torn open and the things he makes (stand-up, books, video) spill out and become the navigation.

name: TRIONN
summary: A dark WebGL stage where the studio's angular logo floats as a wireframe among black shards the visitor can blast; the copy is secondary to the toy.

name: twks
summary: A Geneva agency site set like a Swiss printed sheet: the fold is a black field with the navigation as one horizon line across the exact middle, broken by a single gold object from a client project that turns slowly; then an indented statement, the work on a tight 10px grid, and a fixed black footer where an animal…

name: Typewave
summary: A plugin about type scales sold on a near-black page where flat saturated fields (orange, lime, blue) act as stages for the plugin's own dark interface.

name: UGLYCASH
summary: A money app sold like streetwear: one shouted condensed headline over the phone, then sticker-covered 3D props where feature icons would normally go.

name: Uncle Rudy
summary: A grumpy cartoon uncle who insults you is the brand; his stickers and roast notifications carry the page.

name: Uni
summary: The product lives in the laptop notch, so the page's navigation is a black notch and the hero is a laptop outline whose notch opens into the app.

name: United Carriers
summary: One operator covering every route, shown literally as a dot-matrix globe with route arcs and country tags beside a blunt three-line promise.

name: USAvionix
summary: A maker of autonomous jet drones explains its product as a single mission played out on scroll: one pinned WebGL camera flies from a lone drone over forested mountains to a swarm, to detection overlays and then to a dark tactical map, while a console readout runs at the edges and three status colours (observed,…

name: Vectr
summary: An industrial staffing service tells its process as a flight over a miniature clay world: one fixed WebGL diorama of plants, warehouses, wind turbines and tiny workers in a single matte pale blue that matches the page ground, crossed by a glowing blue trail that runs from a headquarters building past a campus and a…

name: Vero New-York
summary: Treat a keepsake like couture: a slow close-up film opens, then a white 3D sculpture of a dress stays pinned at centre while one sentence in mixed capitals and italics passes over it.

name: Vessa
summary: A brand-guidelines tool that frames its live demo inside an electric-blue dithered pixel field and marks the whole page with dashed artboard guides and corner handles.

name: Vestris
summary: Dry title-settlement software wrapped in a calm painted countryside: gouache-style foliage and skies frame the product so paperwork feels pastoral.

name: Viewport
summary: The page is drawn inside a glowing blue rounded frame: the product's own viewport icon scaled up to the size of the browser window.

name: Warm & Fuzzy
summary: A showreel-first studio site in which every section takes one flat, loud colour (blue, black, yellow) under heavy grotesk type and a chunky custom wordmark.

name: WeekSync
summary: The page is a paper coupon: a dotted cut line with a scissors icon frames the viewport, and on scroll the navigation rail is cut free while the rest of the sheet tilts and falls away.

name: White Desert
summary: One word, the destination, set a third of the screen tall over footage like a film title card; sheer scale stands in for remoteness.

name: wild
summary: A studio essay on craft versus AI in which everything decorative is drawn on one square-pixel grid: the hero heatmap, the icons, the diagrams, the marquee lettering and the footer equaliser.

name: Woblo
summary: The landing page is inspected by its own product: the headline wears the extension's selection box, element-size tag and colour-palette tooltip.

name: Zara Webb
summary: A one-woman newborn-care practice presented like a hand-made keepsake: a mascot rabbit, scalloped and flower-shaped cut-outs, candid film photographs.

name: Black and crimson
summary: Black with off-white text and mid-grey texture takes nearly the whole page, and the last sections may invert to off-white with black type. Deep crimson is scattered sparingly: a few characters in a heading, a slider fill, the one button.

name: Blue, red, black
summary: Three flat poster colours each own whole sections: electric blue, red-orange and black, with white for the areas that show the product. No tints sit between them, and blue is the button colour on white.

name: Blush and aubergine
summary: Blush pink and dark aubergine alternate as full fields and serve as each other's text colour, in roughly equal shares. There is no third colour: the button is a solid block of whichever of the two is not the ground.

name: Blush, sage, slate
summary: Slate blue-grey, sage and blush share the page as soft flat blocks, one per chapter or menu tile, with dark type; one deep olive block anchors the close with pale type. Olive is also the button colour, and photographs of sea and sky do the rest.

name: Bone, green, chocolate
summary: Bone ground with chocolate-brown text takes most of the page. The green is spent on one large flat block, about a third of a screen, and on the button; all other colour comes from photographs.

name: Bottle green, gold
summary: Bottle green covers the page and warm gold sets all the type, with panels one step lighter than the ground. The button is solid gold with green text, and photographs are kept dark and warm so the pair is not disturbed.

name: Bottle ink, yellow
summary: Off-white ground with all type in a near-black bottle green instead of black. Yellow is the only saturated note: the button or one small object on most screens, and one later section that turns fully yellow.

name: Bubblegum and lime
summary: A flat bubblegum pink field with black type from top to bottom. Fluorescent lime is the action colour only: the menu button, one highlighter swipe behind a word and the main button.

name: Burgundy and bubblegum
summary: Deep burgundy is the ground for the whole page and bubblegum pink sets every word on it. The button and the active state of a control are solid pink with burgundy type; product photographs supply any other colour.

name: Candy chapters
summary: Each section owns one flat candy colour: yellow first, then white, pink, cyan and orange, with all type in black. Magenta is kept for buttons alone.

name: Candy on black
summary: Black ground and dark photographs take nearly all of the surface. The only flat colour is a solid block behind each title, which takes a new candy pastel per project (mint, cyan, lemon, orange, cornflower); cyan is the default for the button.

name: Card pastels
summary: Neutral paper ground and black type, with each card or tile given its own flat pastel (periwinkle, lime, amber or cyan), never two alike side by side. Magenta is reserved for the logo, the email address and text links.

name: Carmine field
summary: A deep red field bookends or fills the page, with white type and pale pink secondary lines; work shown in between sits on flat charcoal so it keeps its own colours. The button is a pale pink block with red type.

name: Charcoal and primaries
summary: A charcoal ground holds flat poster primaries assigned to whole panels: red, blue, teal green and yellow, each placed against a different one. Type is white, or black on yellow; teal green is the button colour on charcoal.

name: Charcoal and sage
summary: Charcoal holds the page with off-white text, and one section may flip to a pale concrete tone with dark text. Colour comes from the photographs; grey sage is used for the single button and the active state of a control.

name: Cobalt field
summary: One electric cobalt fills everything, with white and pale-blue type; photographs are tinted into blue monotone or kept as small thumbnails. A single yellow dot or button is the only other colour on the page.

name: Cobalt on sand
summary: Sand paper and one cobalt do everything: text, drawings and solid shapes are all the same blue. The button is a cobalt block with sand-coloured type, and no black or second hue is used.

name: Cool grey, cobalt
summary: Cool pale grey holds the page with near-black type and nothing else tinted. Cobalt starts as the button and one highlighted sentence, takes one whole section as a flat field with white text, then returns as a single button block.

name: Forest and lime
summary: Forest green, black and white sections alternate, with forest green holding the most; photographs stay in moss greens and stone browns. Pale lime sits on small squares only, such as arrow buttons and the closing wordmark.

name: Frost and slate
summary: Cool white and one paler blue-grey step hold everything, with type in dark slate instead of black. Teal appears once per screen at most, as the primary button or one small detail beside the product photograph.

name: Graphite and orange
summary: Graphite and cool light-grey sections alternate, graphite taking about two thirds, and photographs are desaturated so nothing competes. Safety orange marks the buttons, one thick solid bar across the top of the page and the highlighted item in a list or chart.

name: Green-black and bone
summary: Bone type on green-black from top to bottom, with panels and drawn details barely lighter than the ground so photographs supply the colour. Pale jade is for the booking or contact button alone.

name: Grey, mint, orange
summary: Black on white to start, then whole sections flood with flat mid-grey, acid mint and orange in turn. Photographs inside a flooded section are shown in black-and-white, and mint is also the button colour on white and black.

name: Greys and mint
summary: White, near-black and two greys fill a board of flat tiles. Mint floods a few whole tiles (one statement, one figure, the closing call to action) and appears nowhere else.

name: Lunar and bronze
summary: Soft black holds the page with panels one step lighter, white text and grey secondary lines, so photographs supply all the colour. Muted bronze goes on small markers and the one button only.

name: Mint and pink
summary: Near-white base with black type; mint and pink are the only two colours and each stands for one side of the product. They first appear as small circles, then as full-screen section fields, and deep green is used only for the button.

name: Mustard and black
summary: One warm mustard field for the whole page with black ink only. Royal blue is the single interruption, kept to a sliver along one edge or one small button.

name: Navy and pink
summary: One navy field runs the entire page. Pink does everything else, from the name and headings to body text, and fills one solid button.

name: Navy on white
summary: Pure white pages with navy type sit between full-bleed photographs, opening on near-black and closing on a warm grey footer. Tangerine is one small tab or button, never larger than a thumbnail.

name: Newsprint and brass
summary: Warm paper grey with near-black type holds the upper page, then whole sections flip to near-black with paper-grey type; no section is tinted. Brass yellow marks one small detail per screen, such as the button or a single word.

name: Night and cornflower
summary: Blue-black ground and slate panels with silver-white text fill the page; no section changes colour. Cornflower blue marks the buttons and at most one word in a heading.

name: Olive on bone
summary: A bone page with every word, large or small, in one olive green; the footer inverts to a solid olive field with bone text. Photography supplies all other colour, and the button is the same olive, filled.

name: Orange and black
summary: Hot orange is the page: one flat field with blue-black type, flipping at a hard horizontal seam to a white section when the content needs a rest. The button is a solid block of the same blue-black with orange text, and every other colour comes from the objects shown.

name: Orange, sky, lime
summary: The page ground changes as you read: orange first, then sky blue, then acid lime at the end, with one near-black band between; type stays black on all three colours. Crimson is one small button per field.

name: Oxblood and grey
summary: Deep red text on grey paper holds most of the page, then pale grey text on a solid red field takes one long section and the footer. Photographs are desaturated so nothing breaks the pair, and the button is a solid red block.

name: Plum-black and pink
summary: Near-black and plum at the top and bottom bracket a white middle with navy-black text. Hot pink is reserved for primary buttons, bars in charts and map markers; it never fills a section.

name: Post red, mustard
summary: Post red and bone alternate as full section fields, with red holding the opening and the close. Mustard, slate blue and maroon are kept for whole card frames, and slate blue also fills the one button.

name: Poster chapters
summary: Each chapter takes one flat field in turn (coral red, near-black, bone, green, yellow) with black or bone type and no tints between them. Green doubles as the accent for the one button when the ground is bone or black.

name: Putty and black
summary: Warm putty covers the page and pure black handles all type and the main shapes. The only tint in the interface is teal, used for the one button or a single marker placed near the photographs.

name: Report blocks
summary: A white base with flat blocks of orange, sage, acid yellow and black assigned to whole modules: figure tiles, quote panels and chapter bands. Text is black on every colour and off-white on black, and orange is also the button colour.

name: Rose grey, green
summary: A single rosy grey covers the page from top to bottom with brown-black text and grey secondary lines; images are kept greyscale. Green appears only on the current-page link and on one button in the footer.

name: Sand and moss
summary: Sand grey holds the page with charcoal type, and one deep leaf-green band may close it. Moss green is reserved for buttons; brighter greens and blues arrive only through photographs.

name: Sheet and biro
summary: White holds the whole page with black type, one grey for secondary lines and a pale grey step for tiles and inputs; the footer may invert to black. Blue is the colour of text links and the one button, and nothing else is tinted.

name: Signal red, white
summary: White ground, black text and paper grey for filled panels, with one full black band allowed. Signal red is the only colour in the interface: one word in a headline, a few solid blocks, or the button.

name: Sky and navy
summary: Sky blue sits behind everything, white cards lie on top of it, and navy handles all text and the footer. Orange is for buttons and one highlighted word, so orange against blue is the single clash on the page.

name: Sky and sand
summary: Sky blue and sand yellow are the constant ground, each holding whole sections, with black text throughout. Saturated colour arrives only as small solid objects, and magenta is kept for the contact card and its button.

name: Soot and lime
summary: A soot-black opening and close bracket white middle sections, all in black, white and grey. Pale lime is the single action colour: every button, and at most one headline set in it on the dark ground.

name: Stone and blueprint
summary: Stone paper carries the whole page with near-black and grey text. One image at a time is printed in the accent blue as its only ink, and the same blue fills the single button.

name: Studio grey
summary: One mid grey serves as both page and studio backdrop, so the photographed object seems to stand on the page itself; type is black and one black band comes late. Colour comes only from the product, and racing green is for the single button.

name: Swapping pastels
summary: One flat pastel is the whole background and it swaps per project or chapter: periwinkle, pink, sand, sage, peach. Type and one solid box stay near-black on all five, and dark teal is only for the button.

name: Teal on paper
summary: Cool white paper and a single teal used for every word, shape and button, with no black anywhere. The accent is that same teal filled solid, for the button and for one inverted band with paper-coloured type.

name: Three stones
summary: Three close stone tones share the interface: the lightest for the page, the middle one for panels, the darkest for a single band, all with charcoal type. Saturated colour is left to the photographs and their backdrops; the grey-green fills the button only.

name: Tobacco and olive
summary: Tobacco brown fills the page with bone type, and photographs stay in browns and ochre. One olive block holds the main text or the button, and a single ochre band may break the brown once.

name: Ultramarine and yellow
summary: Each section is one flat field in sequence: ultramarine, black, yellow, then ultramarine again, with white type on blue and black, and black type on yellow. Green is the only small accent and never grows larger than a button.

name: Walnut and tan
summary: Dark walnut holds the opening and the close with bone type, and the middle of the page may turn to flat tan around honey-lit photographs. There is no bright accent: tan is the fill for the one button on walnut.

name: Warm black, gold
summary: Warm near-black fills the page and photographs sit bright against it, with pure white small type; panels warm to a brown-black. Gold is for one text link or small button per screen, never a field.

name: Albert Sans
summary: A geometric grotesque with Scandinavian restraint: round letters, even colour, nothing decorative. Suits logistics, health, property and corporate sites that need to look clear and dependable.

name: Anton / Work Sans
summary: Compressed heavy capitals stacked tight, with a neutral grotesque kept small beneath. Suits fashion drops, sport, nightlife and any page built as a poster.

name: Archivo
summary: A sturdy grotesque kept at regular weight even at 88px, so the page reads as composed rather than loud. Suits finance, infrastructure and research pages that need to look sober and current.

name: Archivo
summary: One variable family pushed to its narrowest, heaviest setting for headlines and relaxed to normal width for text, so display and body share a skeleton. Suits sportswear, campaigns and fintech pages that speak in capitals.

name: Barlow Condensed / Barlow
summary: Road-sign condensed type with squared curves, bold but not compressed into a wall, with its normal-width sibling for text. Suits logistics, motorsport, hardware and directories with many short titles.

name: Bebas Neue / EB Garamond
summary: Huge condensed capitals against a light old-style serif with italics: an industrial voice and a literary one, with a twenty-fold size gap between them. Suits crafted physical products, spirits, outdoor goods and hospitality.

name: Besley / Libre Franklin
summary: A fat Clarendon with ball terminals and bracketed slabs over a plain gothic, the look of a nineteenth-century bill poster. Suits breweries, barbers, markets, fairs and heritage goods.

name: Big Shoulders / Public Sans
summary: A tall American gothic taken from city signage, blunt and civic, over a plain public-service sans. Suits culture indexes, community projects, bars, sport clubs and local campaigns.

name: Bodoni Moda / Jost
summary: A true didone with hairline serifs and vertical stress over a light geometric sans, the classic fashion-magazine pairing. Suits luxury property, jewellery, fragrance and fashion.

name: Boska
summary: A high-contrast serif with pointed serifs and a lively italic, used roman and italic together at one size. Suits perfume, jewellery, lodges, weddings and other occasions for ceremony.

name: Bricolage Grotesque
summary: A grotesk with visible stroke contrast and slightly irregular curves, so headings look drawn rather than engineered. Suits reports, consultancies and design-led software that want warmth without a serif.

name: Cabinet Grotesk
summary: A heavy sans with tight joins and an eccentric lowercase, friendly but loud. Suits bookshops, food, consumer subscriptions and marketing studios.

name: Chillax
summary: A soft geometric sans with wide round letters and relaxed joins, warm at semibold and easy at text size. Suits consumer apps, community products, cafes and small friendly brands.

name: Chivo
summary: A black grotesque in capitals with letters nearly colliding, and only two sizes on the page: enormous and small. Suits agencies, city and culture projects and musicians who want the type to land like a headline.

name: Clash Grotesk
summary: A slightly narrow neo-grotesk with closed apertures, used at regular weight from marquee size down to paragraphs. Suits agencies and digital studios that want large type without heaviness.

name: EB Garamond
summary: A humanist Garamond in roman and italic at two modest sizes, with no capitals and no bold. Suits set designers, antique dealers, wine, publishers and portfolios that whisper.

name: Epilogue
summary: A broad black grotesque with a slightly uneven rhythm, at its best as a name set very large in mixed case. Suits entertainers, podcasts, consumer apps and blunt SaaS pages; emphasis comes from colour, not from a change of weight.

name: Erode
summary: A serif with chiselled, angular curves and wedge serifs, sharp at display size and firm in text. Suits studios, galleries, advisory firms and written guides.

name: Gambarino / General Sans
summary: A narrow, sharp display serif for headlines against a small plain sans: a five-to-one jump with nothing between. Suits agencies, bakeries and restaurants, fashion and editorial brands.

name: General Sans
summary: A grotesk with slightly geometric bowls, set bold and very large against plain 16px text with nothing in between. Suits studios, type and product launches, and finance or tech brands that lead with the name.

name: Hanken Grotesk
summary: Medium-weight grotesk statements at one large size against caption-size text: a two-size system with no bold. Suits portfolios, agencies and tools that speak in short declarative lines.

name: Imbue / Albert Sans
summary: A tall, condensed high-contrast serif whose capitals read like a masthead or a shop fascia. Suits residences, hotels, restaurants and wine, where a short name can stand floor to ceiling.

name: Jost
summary: The pointed, circular geometry of the 1920s in bold capitals, with the same family at reading size. Suits space, science, museums, architecture and anything that should feel like a mid-century poster.

name: League Spartan / Figtree
summary: A compact bold geometric with a low waist, punchy in short lowercase lines, over a friendly open text sans. Suits newsletters, consumer products, creators and small shops.

name: Libre Franklin / Source Serif 4
summary: An American gothic for headings over a sober transitional serif for reading, the pairing of a newspaper front page. Suits essays, annual reports, archives and finance pages that have real paragraphs.

name: Literata
summary: A sturdy screen-reading serif with a large x-height; headings are simply the text face at medium weight and a larger size. Suits essays, reports, newsletters and knowledge products.

name: Newsreader
summary: One news serif with optical sizes: light and very tight when huge, open and bookish at 18px. Suits long-form stories, culture pieces, journals and research write-ups.

name: Panchang / Switzer
summary: A flat-sided extended grotesk in heavy capitals, wide enough that two words fill the screen, with a neutral sans kept small. Suits portfolios, real estate, travel and brand sites that want a broad, confident wordmark.

name: Pilcrow Rounded
summary: A sturdy sans with fully rounded stroke ends, set bold and tight in lowercase with one small size for everything else. Suits toys, gadgets, cosmetics and other objects with soft moulded edges.

name: Red Hat Display / Red Hat Text
summary: A geometric black with round bowls and flat terminals, cleaner and more even than a grotesque at the same weight. Suits fintech, apps and portfolios that want heavy type with a tidy, technical finish.

name: Rokkitt / Literata
summary: Narrow geometric slab capitals as a tall title block, then a bookish serif for a long essay beneath. Suits manufacturing, trades, manifestos and industrial history.

name: Roundo
summary: A rounded geometric sans at medium weight and a generous text size, gentle without looking childish. Suits wellness, home goods, family apps and everyday money tools.

name: Schibsted Grotesk
summary: A compact, warm grotesk set heavy with letters almost touching; small text stays in the same family at semibold. Suits music, events and culture pages where the type is the image.

name: Sentient
summary: A soft, low-contrast serif in a light weight, more book than fashion magazine, large and calm in sentence case. Suits outdoor and craft products, restaurants, cameras and slow consumer goods.

name: Stack Sans Headline / Stack Sans Text
summary: A geometric sans in a light weight at large size, soft and exact at once, with its text cut underneath. Suits consumer apps, utilities and developer tools that want to feel calm and modern.

name: STIX Two Text
summary: The plain Times-style roman of a typed document, slightly tightened and never larger than a few vw. Suits vehicles and tools presented dryly, artists' pages, investment memos and anything meant to look undesigned on purpose.

name: Switzer
summary: One neo-grotesk doing everything: semibold headings pulled tight, small regular text, no capitals and no second voice. Suits software, hardware and studio pages that want to look exact and unshowy.

name: Switzer
summary: A single roman weight of a Swiss neo-grotesk at two or three modest sizes; position and grey value do the work that size and bold usually do. Suits architects, galleries, studios and any quiet page where photographs carry the scale.

name: TikTok Sans
summary: One variable grotesk stretched wide and bold for the headline and the closing statement, then returned to normal width for reading. Suits personal portfolios, apps and tech brands that want width without a second family.

name: Unbounded / Onest
summary: A wide display sans built from rounded squares, heavy and a little architectural, beside a clean text grotesk. Suits architecture indexes, watches, mobility and events that want a title with a constructed feel.

name: Work Sans
summary: A light grotesque with open, slightly old-fashioned shapes; large headings look airy and the text weight beneath stays easy to read. Suits AI and research products, fashion houses and calm brand sites.

name: Young Serif / Source Serif 4
summary: A heavy, round old-style headline face with soft bracketed serifs over a clear transitional text serif. Suits essays, food, independent publishers and personal sites that want warmth with weight.

name: Zilla Slab
summary: A contemporary slab with smooth curves and unbracketed serifs, even enough to carry headings and paragraphs alike. Suits developer tools, personal sites, open-source and nonprofit projects.

name: Zodiak / Hanken Grotesk
summary: Hairline serif capitals set large enough that the thin strokes read as drawing, with a small neutral sans for everything practical. Suits lodges, spas, architecture and interiors; keep it on flat pale or dark fields where the strokes have full contrast.

name: Anchored text, specimen half
summary: The viewport is split exactly in half by two flat tones that meet at a clean vertical edge: the ground on the left, a palette colour on the right.

name: Card over a dim room
summary: A full-bleed, low-key photograph of the room fills the viewport, darkened with filter: brightness(0.7) so it reads as atmosphere.

name: Colour field, two-ink statement
summary: One saturated flat colour covers the whole viewport; there is no navigation bar and no image.

name: Column on one line
summary: A warm off-white page that is more than 80% empty.

name: Control that reads the page
summary: A near-black or deep neutral ground split into two halves by tone alone: the right half is one step lighter than the left, and they meet at a clean vertical edge at 50%.

name: Controls on the sentence
summary: A dark flat ground with no logo bar: a 14px wordmark top-left and the single action as an underlined text link top-right, both 28px in.

name: Counter object, wide wordmark
summary: Borrowed from a watch or perfume counter.

name: Film title, bottom edge
summary: One photograph fills the viewport at 100vw by 100svh, object-fit: cover, with its subject in the upper two-thirds and a calmer, darker zone along the bottom.

name: Flush-left shout, seam photograph
summary: Borrowed from a street poster or zine.

name: Fragment on a shaped stage
summary: A neutral ground. The headline occupies the upper-left third: two lines at clamp(52px, 5.2vw, 80px), medium weight, flush left on columns 1–6 at a 40px margin, starting 150px down.

name: Giant cropped shape
summary: A plain ground with one flat shape at enormous scale.

name: Headline across two fields
summary: The viewport is two flat fields meeting at exactly half height: paper above, one saturated colour below, with a hard edge and nothing drawn on it.

name: Inset photograph, crossing wordmark
summary: One deep, dark flat field.

name: Invitation card, cropped
summary: A flat field of one soft colour fills the viewport.

name: Line-up on an arc
summary: For a range: flavours, colourways, editions, sizes.

name: Lit strip, four corners
summary: One near-black field with a single lit band.

name: Menu column, sticky photograph
summary: The viewport is two panels of equal width with a 12px gap between them and 12px outer margins, both with a 20px radius.

name: Mosaic masthead, title on axis
summary: The top 52% of the viewport is a full-width masthead band built as a gutterless mosaic: a CSS grid of 6 columns and 2 rows in which four cells are photographs (object-fit: cover, all greyscale via filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)) and the rest are flat tiles in two or three palette colours.

name: Name across the middle
summary: Paper and ink only; no picture on the first screen.

name: Name band and rails
summary: One viewport filled completely with tiles on 8px gaps and 8px margins.

name: Name split to corners
summary: The name is cut into two halves that stay pinned to opposite corners while the page passes between them.

name: Name under a photograph
summary: A full-bleed photograph fills the top 58% of the 1440×900 viewport, touching the top, left and right edges, object-fit: cover, with its focal point in the upper two-thirds.

name: Narrow talk, wide headline
summary: An asymmetric sheet on one flat paper-grey ground, divided at 34% of the width by alignment only.

name: Navigation on the midline
summary: One photograph or muted film fills the viewport at 100vw by 100svh, object-fit: cover, framed so the middle of the screen cuts the subject: a face or a skyline in the upper half, hands or ground in the lower.

name: Object cropped by three edges
summary: A flat off-white or single bold colour field with no navigation bar: only a small wordmark top-right at 24px and the single action fixed bottom-right as a solid rectangular button.

name: Object on the seam
summary: A white or very pale page organised by one change of tone.

name: Object splits the headline
summary: One deep, flat ground colour.

name: One word, cropped
summary: A single word is the whole composition, set so large that the viewport crops it.

name: Photograph for a letter
summary: A flat white or pale ground, about 85% empty.

name: Pinned title over portraits
summary: A pale flat ground. The title runs on one line of extra-bold uppercase at clamp(90px, 10vw, 160px), centred, spanning about 82% of the width, its cap line 120px from the top.

name: Ring of frames around the headline
summary: One near-black or deep flat field.

name: Sentence split by a frame
summary: A white or pale ground.

name: Sentence with a photo strip
summary: A warm flat ground with no navigation bar.

name: Sheet with a text cell
summary: The whole viewport is a sheet of photographs: six columns with 12px gaps and 12px outer margins, each column a vertical stack of frames at natural ratios with square corners.

name: Shouted headline, rising photograph
summary: Borrowed from a fashion drop.

name: Single object on a plinth
summary: An off-white screen that is about 80% empty and does not need to scroll.

name: Single specimen with name list
summary: Borrowed from a museum plinth.

name: Small name, open sky
summary: A single photograph fills the viewport edge to edge with no frame: choose one whose upper 45% is sky, wall or water with nothing in it and whose subject sits low and off-centre.

name: Specimen wall, docked panel
summary: There is no header and no display headline: the whole viewport is a wall of specimens.

name: Square over a moving line
summary: A white or pale flat ground.

name: Stacked name, two inks
summary: One saturated flat field covers the whole 1440×900 viewport and there is no image.

name: Statement beside specimen mosaic
summary: The viewport is split 50/50 by tone alone: the left half is the page ground, the right half a field one step darker, meeting at a clean vertical edge with no line.

name: Stepped title, two photographs
summary: A pale neutral ground with 6vw side margins on a 12-column grid.

name: Striped card beside the room
summary: The viewport is split 50/50 with a 12px gap and 12px outer margins.

name: Swatch column beside the view
summary: A 10px frame of paper colour surrounds the screen.

name: Tabbed folder stack
summary: A dark flat ground. A slim top row at 24px holds the wordmark dead centre and one text link far right at 15px.

name: Text band, then sheet
summary: A black or white field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins and 14px gaps.

name: Three prints, one line
summary: Photographs lead and the type stays small.

name: Title from the top edge to the bottom edge
summary: One full-bleed photograph or film at 100vw by 100svh, with a horizon near half height and empty sky or darkness above.

name: Title in the sky, line on the horizon
summary: One wide photograph or render fills the viewport, chosen with the subject in the lower 55% and open sky, fog or a plain wall above it.

name: Two doors on a dark wall
summary: For a subject with two halves a visitor must choose between: two exhibitions, two audiences, two places, two collections.

name: Two prints in darkness
summary: One near-black field with a slight colour tint, about 75% of it left empty.

name: Two-by-two board
summary: A board with 8px outer margins and 8px gaps throughout; every tile is a filled rectangle with one shared radius (0 or 8px).

name: Two-line statement, full width
summary: Paper and ink only; no image.

name: View with two cards in the corner
summary: One photograph or muted film fills the viewport, object-fit: cover, with the subject in the right half.

name: Void, then statement on axis
summary: A deliberate void: the upper 60% of the viewport holds nothing but the top row.

name: Waterline headline
summary: Two flat fields fill the viewport and meet at exactly half height: the upper one paper or white, the lower one a saturated palette colour.

name: Window that opens to the edges
summary: A flat paper or pale ground, and one picture seen through a small window that becomes the whole screen as the page scrolls.

name: A band per question
summary: Each question owns a full-bleed band, and the bands alternate between two flat tones (ground and one step away, or two palette colours with their assigned inks) and butt together with no gap.

name: A footer of tiles
summary: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used.

name: A plain sentence, one action
summary: The page ends on an almost empty screen.

name: A sentence with a blank
summary: The closing sentence has a gap in it, and the gap is the form.

name: A single quiet line
summary: No footer block at all.

name: Accordion of filled tiles
summary: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, position: sticky; top: 96px so it stays while the list scrolls past.

name: Accordion of tinted panels
summary: A two-column introduction, then one horizontal accordion.

name: Address in display rows
summary: The contact block is a stack of five full-width rows, every one set at the same size, clamp(44px, 6vw, 88px), regular weight, left-aligned with a 20px inset and leading 1.0: the building or venue name, the street, the city with postcode, the opening hours as one compact line, the phone number.

name: Answers as reading text
summary: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme.

name: Band of unequal panels
summary: A modest heading, then one wide band of pictures.

name: Bars standing on the edge
summary: The product's own chart, drawn in HTML, is the whole section.

name: Big names, fixed preview
summary: Project names are the index.

name: Book-spine index
summary: The complete index in the footprint of a banner.

name: Call and response column
summary: The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis.

name: Capabilities as a menu
summary: The capabilities are set as a printed menu or price list.

name: Capabilities at poster scale
summary: No images. The heading, two to four words, is the first line of the list itself, set at the same size as the items but in the soft ink, so no separate title sits above.

name: Cards crossing a held photograph
summary: A wrapper about 350svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh.

name: Cards that fold into spines
summary: For a journal, a run of notes or a list of chapters without pictures.

name: Clip-out coupon form
summary: The form is a coupon to cut out.

name: Close-up with column card
summary: A full-bleed close-up photograph, 100vw by 100svh, with nothing over most of it.

name: Close-ups on a board
summary: A board of filled tiles, each a macro view of one small part of the interface.

name: Column aligned on the decimal
summary: A tall column of figures set like a ledger.

name: Columns above, wordmark below
summary: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto).

name: Comparison set as text
summary: A comparison table with no lines and no tick marks.

name: Contact as the headline
summary: A full-bleed field in one saturated palette colour, at least 90svh tall.

name: Day tabs, banded agenda
summary: A two-line heading at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), first line in the soft ink and second in full ink, with the booking button on the same row at the far right.

name: Dense masonry sheet
summary: A three-line statement at 22px, 30ch wide, sits at the 66% column with 64px of space below it; it is the only large text.

name: Drag row of mixed modules
summary: One horizontal row, 68svh tall, running off both viewport edges with 12px gaps, draggable and scrollable sideways (overflow-x: auto, scroll-snap-type: x proximity, scrollbar hidden).

name: Drag row of moments
summary: A story told left to right.

name: Drag through the stages
summary: A 50/50 split, 88svh tall: two flat fields meeting on a clean vertical edge, and one slider that drives both.

name: Edge-to-edge heavy paragraph
summary: A full-bleed flat colour field, at least 90svh tall, filled by one paragraph and nothing else.

name: Figure on the photograph's edge
summary: One full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 88svh, and one figure set on it the way a film title sits on a frame.

name: Figure set by a slider
summary: The number is the visitor's own.

name: Figures inside a sentence
summary: The numbers are written into prose and the prose is set at display size.

name: First step, already open
summary: The page ends with the product's first screen already open.

name: Fixed output, live controls
summary: A split the reader operates.

name: Founder's letter
summary: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below.

name: Four cards dealt into a fan
summary: Four values, rules or features, each on a card dealt onto the table as the page scrolls.

name: Frame run, one lifted
summary: Columns 1–3 are a nearly empty column: the heading (two to four words at 24–28px) at the top, a link under it, and one or two short notes at 15px much further down, each level with the frame it describes.

name: Full panels, one midline row
summary: Four to seven consecutive panels, each 100vw by 100svh, butted together with no gap.

name: Full-bleed sequence, text interlocked
summary: Three photographs, each 100vw by 100svh, shown one after another with nothing between them.

name: Giant command list
summary: The capabilities are set as the product's own command menu, scaled up until it is the section; the root is marked data-ui.

name: Giant title, uneven wall
summary: A one- or two-word title in capitals at clamp(72px, 9vw, 136px), leading 0.9, sits flush left at the 16px margin; on its baseline at the far right, one underlined link at 15px to the full archive.

name: Giant word, filled bar rows
summary: Sized for a reading column 520–640px wide, or centred at that width on a full page.

name: Heading captions a panorama
summary: The section is exactly 100svh.

name: Headline crossing onto a photograph
summary: A white or pale ground.

name: Headline you can type
summary: The section's headline is an input.

name: Input half, output half
summary: Two flat fields meet on a vertical edge at 50vw, each 90svh tall, no gap.

name: Inset panel, shaped portrait
summary: A deep-toned panel inset 20px from the page edges with a 12px radius, about 110svh tall, overflow: hidden.

name: Invitation over a cropped name
summary: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour.

name: Itinerary on a slip
summary: The process is printed as an itinerary or receipt.

name: Large marks on tiles
summary: A board of filled tiles, four across and two or three rows deep, with 8px gaps, spanning the full content width.

name: Large questions, answers beside
summary: Every answer is open; nothing collapses.

name: Last photograph, text beside
summary: A final full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 90svh, chosen so its subject sits in the left half and its right half is calm.

name: Lead line over four columns
summary: Two parts on one 12-column grid with 20px margins.

name: Lead quote, corner quotes
summary: A single field one viewport tall (min-height 100svh), usually the darkest tone of the palette.

name: Line-up at one type size
summary: A full-bleed flat section.

name: Lines that step across
summary: The sequence is written, not counted.

name: Lit panel, dark row
summary: One dark field, 96svh tall.

name: Live demo with controls
summary: One filled panel, 680–760px wide and about 640px tall, radius 12px, in a tone clearly darker or lighter than the ground, placed on the text column's left edge or centred, with at least 15vh of empty ground above and below.

name: Loose scatter with pauses
summary: One word as heading at 32–40px, top-left on the margin.

name: Many into one
summary: A diagram drawn with one repeated shape instead of arrows.

name: Mosaic of unlike tiles
summary: A 12-column grid with 8px gaps and rows of 96px, filled with no empty cells and no outlines.

name: Name across the last photograph
summary: The footer is the page's last photograph, full-bleed at 100vw by 100svh, darkened evenly with filter: brightness(0.62) so paper-coloured type reads everywhere on it.

name: Name block, quote block
summary: Two flat blocks butt together across the full width with no gap, about 70svh tall, built as a two-column grid (5fr 7fr) whose cells stretch to equal height.

name: Name first, places under it
summary: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it.

name: Names as one paragraph
summary: All project or client names run together as one paragraph at poster scale: 10–18 names at clamp(40px, 5.2vw, 78px), leading 1.1, flowing inline across the full width between 24px margins and wrapping where they fall, five to seven lines in all.

name: Names as one sentence
summary: Client, press or partner names are written out as one run-on sentence and set large: clamp(40px, 5vw, 76px), leading 1.0, flush left across all twelve columns, wrapping naturally over five to seven lines.

name: Names passing a held square
summary: A flat ground and one centred column of very large names: eight to fourteen project or product names in condensed capitals at clamp(96px, 14vw, 200px), leading 0.85, one per line and each line centred, so long names run nearly to the margins and short ones leave wide ground either side.

name: Names running off the edges
summary: A full-bleed band in a flat colour, about 34vh tall, holding a single line of names that is cropped by both viewport edges.

name: Narrow column, empty field
summary: A single text column 300–340px wide, its left edge at 15% of the viewport width, starting 64px below the section top.

name: Object in front of type
summary: Type and object share one space instead of sitting side by side.

name: Object on a disc
summary: One section about a viewport tall on a plain ground.

name: Object riding down the schedule
summary: A schedule of dated events (races, concerts, tastings, departures) with the subject's own object travelling down it.

name: One card, four fields
summary: Four flat colour fields stand side by side across the full viewport, each 25vw wide and 84svh tall, butted together with no gaps; neighbours differ clearly in lightness.

name: One control, blown up
summary: A flat saturated field, full-bleed and 92svh tall, holds one working control from the product: the toggle, slider, segmented switch or record button the whole product turns on.

name: One field, nothing else
summary: The whole section is one prompt and one field in a column 520px wide, on the page's text column line or centred, with 200px of empty ground above and 160px below.

name: One figure owns the screen
summary: One number, one screen.

name: One frame, contents change
summary: Instead of many pictures side by side, one frame stays in place and its contents change.

name: One frame, three distances
summary: A wrapper 300vh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh.

name: One image across tiles
summary: One photograph is cut across a board of tiles.

name: One item per poster line
summary: A short list set as a poster.

name: One long letter
summary: A single testimonial given room to be read, set like a letter.

name: One plan as a sentence
summary: The whole offer is one sentence of five to seven short words that contains the price, set at 8–9vw across the full width on two lines, leading 0.95, flush left; it replaces any heading.

name: One quiet logo row
summary: Only for real logos supplied by the project; if none are supplied, set the names in the text face at 22px in the same row and never draw stand-ins.

name: One row, three states
summary: The product's central row (a task, a transaction, a message, a deploy) is shown three times, one directly beneath the other, in three states: as it arrives, with the pointer on it and its actions revealed, and finished.

name: One scene, stepping statements
summary: A wrapper 350–450vh tall holds a sticky full-bleed photograph (100vw by 100svh) with a calm, symmetrical subject and a clear upper third; a neutral dark scrim covers only that upper third.

name: One slide, two neighbours
summary: Each project is one band the full width of the viewport.

name: One strip per project
summary: The left 13% of the width is a position: sticky column holding the section name at 28px and, beneath it, two text filters at 15px, the active one in full ink.

name: One verb at a time
summary: Three to five full-bleed panels, each 100svh tall, stacked with no gap; each is one stage and holds one photograph covering it.

name: One word is the button
summary: The entire band is one link.

name: One-size name columns
summary: Pure text at one size.

name: Output index, live sheet
summary: For products that make documents: invoices, reports, emails, statements.

name: Output slips along the edge
summary: For subjects whose result is a piece of text or paper: a receipt, a note, a ticket, a written line.

name: Oversized visual, small cluster
summary: One project per block, three or four blocks, 140px apart.

name: Panel with margin notes
summary: One tall panel from the product is shown whole, like a plate in a manual, with notes in both margins.

name: Paragraph with picture words
summary: One paragraph does the work of a feature grid.

name: Photo strip, three-cell bar
summary: A saturated flat field about 80svh tall.

name: Photo tiles with label strips
summary: Four columns with 12px gaps; every tile is a photograph with a filled label strip attached directly beneath it, the two forming one object like a print with its swing tag.

name: Photograph half, menu half
summary: A split footer one viewport tall.

name: Photograph with figure tiles
summary: A mosaic without gutters spanning the full width, about 66vw tall in total.

name: Photographs down a diagonal
summary: Three stages, three photographs of different sizes placed along a falling diagonal on the 12-column grid.

name: Photographs gathered round a heading
summary: A band about one screen tall on the plain page ground, used as the page's one deliberate rest.

name: Pinned fragment, changing state
summary: Two columns. Right, columns 7–12: a stage that is position: sticky; top: 14vh, holding one fragment of the real interface at true size on a single flat stage colour, about 520px square.

name: Pinned heading, passing rows
summary: One flat saturated field, full-bleed, as tall as its content.

name: Pinned sentence, photographs pass
summary: A wrapper 300svh tall.

name: Pinned title, portraits pass
summary: A wrapper tall enough for its portraits: about 90svh per person, up to six people.

name: Plain names in columns
summary: A typographic list with no logos.

name: Plan names, one live figure
summary: Plans are a list of names; the price shown belongs to whichever name is selected.

name: Plans as a large table
summary: Two to four plans compared in a table whose type is far larger than a table usually gets.

name: Plans that step up
summary: Three plans as flat colour tiles whose heights step like a bar chart, so the bigger plan is literally bigger.

name: Portrait and offset quotation
summary: A 12-column row on the page ground with wide margins.

name: Portrait as drop cap
summary: No heading. One biography paragraph of 50–80 words is set large at clamp(24px, 2.5vw, 38px), regular weight, leading 1.2, across columns 3–12 of the grid.

name: Portrait on its own ground
summary: One chapter per screen, three to six chapters.

name: Prices like a menu
summary: Prices set the way a good menu sets them.

name: Prints dropped on the headline
summary: A flat colour field 100svh tall.

name: Question at both edges
summary: For a closing choice between two answers: book or ask, this date or that, the tasting or the tour.

name: Question index, one answer
summary: Questions on the left, one answer on the right, and the answer changes as the reader moves through the questions.

name: Questions beside a tall photograph
summary: One field in a deep or pale flat tone, split 5 to 7.

name: Quiet figure lines
summary: Numbers stated without raising the voice.

name: Quiet ledger, side preview
summary: A plain ledger in one column 560px wide whose left edge sits at 22% of the viewport width.

name: Quotation over a photograph
summary: One photograph fills the section edge to edge at 100vw by 90svh with object-fit: cover; choose a frame with a calm lower half.

name: Quotation spread edge to edge
summary: A full-width field with no image.

name: Quote as comment thread
summary: The customer's words arrive the way words arrive inside the product: as a comment.

name: Quotes in the gutters
summary: A sticky stage (position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh) inside a wrapper three or four viewports tall.

name: Quotes on paper slips
summary: A heading of two to four words at about 3vw sits top-left in columns 1–6.

name: Recognition as a table
summary: Awards, press mentions or credits set as a four-column table with no lines.

name: Right-half paragraph, lone photo
summary: No heading. On a 12-column grid with 5vw margins, one statement paragraph of 45–70 words occupies columns 7–12 only, set at clamp(24px, 2.2vw, 34px) with leading 1.25 and a first-line indent of 3em.

name: Rising triptych
summary: A wrapper about 200svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh on the plain page ground.

name: Rows as a board
summary: The product's main list is set like a station departure board.

name: Rows with margin photographs
summary: Everything hangs from one vertical axis at column 5, about 35% of the width.

name: Run-in column
summary: The quietest sequence: one reading column and good typography.

name: Sentence, portrait, two links
summary: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid.

name: Sentences with switches
summary: Four or five capabilities, each one plain sentence of five to eight words about what the product will do for you, each ending in a working switch.

name: Shallow portraits, small quotes
summary: Speakers are shown as wide, shallow crops rather than headshots.

name: Shape-marked small points
summary: For the many minor points that do not deserve a row each.

name: Side facts, wide paragraph
summary: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width.

name: Small frames, wide space
summary: A flat, quiet viewport 100svh tall in which about 70% of the screen is empty.

name: Small index, large picture
summary: A sticky stage of 100svh split 38/62.

name: Small proof beside text
summary: One narrow module repeated four to six times down the page, never alternating sides.

name: Specimens on colour tiles
summary: Each capability is represented by one object photographed alone and shown on a flat colour tile.

name: Square plate, spare text
summary: One flat field split 50/50, at least 88svh tall.

name: Stacked folders with tabs
summary: Projects are filed as folders: four to six full-width flat colour bands stacked so that each shows a 64px strip above the next, built with position: sticky and increasing top offsets (0, 64, 128px) so the bands pile up as the page scrolls.

name: Stacking colour sheets
summary: Three to five capabilities, each a full-width flat colour sheet about 86svh tall with only its top corners rounded at 28px.

name: Stages as one bar
summary: The product's progress bar, enlarged until it spans the page, is the diagram.

name: Staggered fragment cells
summary: A three-column grid of six filled cells with 8px gaps, each cell 420–460px tall and filled one tone off the ground, no outlines.

name: Staggered pairs in empty ground
summary: No heading. Photographs are placed one or two per screen so that more than half of every screen stays empty ground.

name: Staggered tiles, empty cells
summary: A four-column grid with 16px gutters and 5vw margins in which tiles snap to columns but vary in span and height, and some cells are deliberately left empty.

name: Staircase statement
summary: On a flat dark or saturated field one sentence of 12–18 words is broken into five short lines at clamp(36px, 4.4vw, 64px), bold, leading 1.02, marked up as one paragraph (a statement, so it may run past two lines at this size).

name: Statement cell, dark rows
summary: Two halves butted together, each 50vw wide and at least 90svh tall, with no gap.

name: Statement tiles
summary: A board of filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8px outer margins: 12 columns by two rows of 38svh each.

name: Statement with inline thumbnails
summary: A centred statement of 18–28 words, four lines at clamp(32px, 4.2vw, 62px), medium or bold weight, leading 1.12, in a block 60–66% of the viewport wide with 22vh of empty ground above and below.

name: Statement, table pushed right
summary: A heading of four to six words spans the full width on two lines at clamp(40px, 4.5vw, 68px), left-aligned with its first line indented 3vw and leading 0.98.

name: Statements on colour fields
summary: Three or four full-bleed flat colour fields, each 72–80svh tall, butted together with no gap.

name: Stepped figure tiles
summary: Three figures on three tiles that refuse to line up.

name: Sticky photograph, active list
summary: Two columns. The left, columns 1–5, is position: sticky; top: 12vh and holds one photograph or object at 4:5, 34vw wide, unframed on the ground.

name: Tabbed index cards
summary: Questions are filed like cards in a drawer.

name: Team on colour tiles
summary: A one-line heading of two or three words at 28–36px sits top-left; nothing sits to its right.

name: The action tile
summary: The close is one row of the board.

name: The back of the card
summary: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard.

name: The email as display type
summary: The section is 100svh in the inverse of the page's colours.

name: The idea again, inverted
summary: The close flips the page's colours: ink becomes the ground and the ground becomes the ink, across a full-bleed field at least 90svh tall.

name: The itemised receipt
summary: For offers made of parts: a base price plus options, a kit, a bundle.

name: The mark, built large
summary: On a flat colour field, the brand closes the page as a construction rather than as set type.

name: The object returns
summary: The thing shown in the hero comes back once, from another angle, to close the page.

name: The price, very large
summary: One plan, no card. Columns 1–4 hold a heading of two to four words at 28–36px and one paragraph at 17px, top-aligned.

name: The printed guest list
summary: Names are printed on a card, the way a programme lists its patrons or an invitation its hosts.

name: The printed menu sheet
summary: The list is one tall sheet of paper.

name: The reply card
summary: The invitation to act is a printed card lying on the page.

name: The ticket
summary: The price is printed on a ticket.

name: Three photographs, then a field
summary: Two parts with no gap between them.

name: Tiles that grow
summary: Order is carried by size.

name: Title torn at the seam
summary: A wrapper about 95svh tall per project holds a sticky stage of 100svh, split at exactly 50vw into two portrait panes of 720×900px, object-fit: cover, square corners, no gap: two different pictures or loops of the same project (the whole and a detail, before and after).

name: Title, note, facts row
summary: First row: a heading of two to four words in a light weight at clamp(44px, 5vw, 76px) sits on the left margin in columns 1–6; a three-line paragraph at 16px, 260px wide, sits in columns 10–12 with its last line on the heading's baseline.

name: Total and its receipt
summary: A total at giant size, and beside it the slip that adds up to it.

name: Two columns, highlighted words
summary: The story is set as text far larger than anything else on the page: 110–160 words at clamp(22px, 2.1vw, 32px), tight leading 1.18, in the soft ink, flowing through two columns that fill the full width between 24px margins (columns: 2; column-gap: 32px, justified, with hyphenation on).

name: Two giant words compared
summary: No photographs: the thing shown is a pair of words, characters or figures that make the point by comparison (before and after, input and output, ours and the usual).

name: Two objects, two fields
summary: Two panels side by side, each 50vw wide and 92svh tall, in two different flat tones from the palette, meeting on a clean vertical edge with no gap.

name: Two plans, two fields
summary: Two plans stand side by side as two full-height colour fields that meet at a hard vertical edge with no gap: the left field spans columns 1–5, the right 6–12, both 90svh tall and bleeding to the viewport edges.

name: Two-column menu, photo bullets
summary: A menu or catalogue list in which each item has a small cut-out photograph where a bullet would be.

name: Two-ended rows, narrow column
summary: A list in one narrow column, 520px wide, starting at 22% of the viewport width or centred.

name: Visit card on a photograph
summary: A full-bleed photograph of the place, 100vw by 100svh, carries one solid card and nothing else.

name: Wall of word tiles
summary: A gallery that works with no photographs: a four-column grid of identical square cells with 8px gaps running three or more rows, edge to edge with 8px margins.

name: Wide heading, indented questions
summary: A heading of three to five words at about 5.5vw runs from the left margin on one or two lines and is the only large thing in the section.

name: Wide photo, colour tile, facts
summary: Top: a heading of two to four words at clamp(40px, 4vw, 60px) on the left margin, then 24px below it a three-line lead paragraph at 21–22px across columns 1–6.

name: Carried picture
summary: Between the index and a case page, the picture the visitor clicked travels into place as the new page's hero while the old page fades out in 200ms and the new one rises in, all within 480ms, using the browser's own cross-document view transitions with no library and no full-screen curtain.

name: Colour by chapter
summary: Each chapter is its own full-bleed field of one palette colour, so the ground changes exactly at section edges as you scroll, never as a global recolouring of the screen.

name: Curtain footer
summary: The page content slides up like a sheet to uncover the footer waiting beneath it, so the last screen is revealed rather than scrolled to.

name: Drag row
summary: A row of large items wider than the screen that the visitor pulls sideways: native horizontal scrolling with scroll snapping, the first item aligned to the page margin and the last allowed to run off the edge so the row visibly continues.

name: Edge-to-edge marquee
summary: One line of very large type travels sideways across the full width at a slow constant speed, as a band between two sections or as the closing statement.

name: Index with preview
summary: Rows of text are the navigation through the work; pointing at a row brings up its image in one fixed frame and dims the other rows.

name: Ink-fill statement
summary: One statement of three to five lines at 32px or more starts at 45% ink and fills to full ink line by line as it rises from three quarters of the way down the screen to just past half way, so the reading pace follows the scroll.

name: Masked headline
summary: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together.

name: Opening window
summary: A type screen hands over to the one great photograph: the picture first shows as a window about 45% of the width in the middle of a held stage and opens to full-bleed over about one screen of scroll, while the image inside settles from 1.15 scale.

name: Pinned story
summary: One element holds its place with position: sticky (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it.

name: Pushed line
summary: One line of very large type, the name or the claim, is pushed sideways by the scroll rather than by a clock: it travels from 12% right to 12% left of its place while it crosses the screen, linear and locked to the scrollbar, and reads whole at the middle of its run.

name: Rolling figures
summary: For a page whose case is a handful of numbers (a report, a fund, a practice with a founding year): three or four figures at display size roll each digit up to its value once as they come into view, about 1.1 seconds on a strong ease-out, the columns 70ms apart.

name: Scaling wordmark
summary: The giant name responds to the scroll: as the first screen leaves, the wordmark scales down a few percent (or grows from 0.94 to 1 as the footer arrives) on a scroll-linked timeline, so the monument feels heavy.

name: Sheet over a held picture
summary: A full-bleed photograph holds its place for one screen and the next chapter, an opaque sheet in the page ground carrying its heading at the top edge, slides up over it like a page being turned.

name: Shutter image
summary: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest.

name: Sideways gallery
summary: A short set of pictures (eight or fewer: rooms, kitchens, pieces) moves sideways while the vertical scroll holds the stage, one pixel of scroll for one pixel of travel, and the hold ends the moment the last picture reaches the margin.

name: Slow crossfade
summary: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives.

name: Stillness
summary: No showpiece. The page is simply there, instantly, and the discipline is the statement.

name: Accent ladder
summary: One brand hue at full strength only on small marks, and its pale tints doing all the area work: the active nav row, a plan card, badges and progress tracks.

name: Achromatic ledger
summary: The chrome holds no colour at all; money and counts are set in ink, the one chart hue marks the screen's main data element, and the only other hue is a small signal where a figure changed.

name: Data terminal
summary: A research or monitoring screen read in long sessions: cards darker than the ground, tabular digits that stack, signs instead of colour, and every selection marked by the same 1px accent line.

name: Editorial greeting
summary: A personal or team home that opens with a typeset greeting in a centred column; every number below it is set at regular weight on tonal panels.

name: Framed sheet
summary: The app chrome is one tinted L-shaped frame; the work sits on a white sheet with a hairline edge and soft corners, so depth comes from a single tone step and no shadow.

name: Pastel consumer
summary: Categories are coded by pale tints whose ink is the dark of the same hue, all under one large radius, and each headline sum sits inside the card that explains it.

name: True-black flat
summary: Night mode on true black: sidebar, top bar and page share one ground, elevation is a lightness step alone, and colour is confined to data marks.

name: Icon rail
summary: An unlabelled rail of 50-60px carries the brand mark at the top and 15-18px outline icons on a 34-49px pitch; groups are split by 20px hairlines, utilities sit at the bottom.

name: No sidebar
summary: A 46-48px top bar on the page ground over a centred 1088-1208px column; the logo sits exactly on the column's left edge and the bar's right cluster ends near its right edge, so header and content share one column.

name: Open plane
summary: The labelled sidebar sits on the page ground with nothing or one hairline between it and the canvas; there is no top bar, and the page header and cards sit straight on the ground about 32-36px from the top.

name: Ruled T-frame
summary: A 210-240px sidebar and a 64px top bar share one ground, divided only by 1px rules.

name: Tinted frame, white sheet
summary: Sidebar and top bar share one tinted ground with no rule between them, forming an L; the page lives on a white sheet.

name: Balance, actions and assets
summary: One column whose every element snaps to its two edges.

name: Bar list and ranking
summary: A 24/700 title with one factual stat chip beside the actions on the right; underline tabs on a 1px rule; a filter row of compound outlined groups that read as a sentence ('Date Jun 14 - Jul 13 Daily', 'Region United States'), 28px tall and 8px apart.

name: Builder canvas
summary: No global navigation: a 44px top bar on the window ground with no rule (an exit arrow, the object's name at 16/600 with a status pill, and on the right 16px icon buttons on a 40px pitch, a secondary and a near-black primary, split by 1px dividers).

name: Count cards that filter
summary: Above a list, 3-5 equal count cards (61px tall, 12px padding, a 13px grey label over a 16/600 value, 8px gap) are the type filter: the selected card gets a 1.5px accent border and a pale accent fill, and the list below shows that type only.

name: Cover against the minimum

name: Current deploy and health lead
summary: Title row: the project's name as the h1 with a status pill (Healthy, Degraded) and a breadcrumb of team and product above it; repository, branch and a freshness stamp in a 14px grey line under it; the one primary action (Redeploy, or View logs when the latest deploy failed) on the right.

name: Finance home with a pinned accounts column
summary: No page header and no KPI strip: cards start 36px from the top and each headline sum sits in the card that explains it.

name: Generated report
summary: No sidebar; the only chrome is a 47-48px viewer bar with a 1px rule.

name: Inbox triage
summary: Three regions on one ground: the navigation (a 230px sidebar or a 55px rail), the list, and the open item with its details.

name: Insights with share tables
summary: No cards: sections are carried by whitespace and a 16/500 heading with one 14px grey sentence under it saying what the section shows.

name: KPI strip, main chart and a side rail
summary: Title row: a 24px noun or the product's name at 600-700, an optional 14-16px grey line under it, and the one primary action on the right, bottom-aligned with that line.

name: KPIs as the chart's tabs
summary: One card per subject, 8-16px apart: the main chart card runs full width, and any card holding a table of five columns or fewer, or a short list, pairs with its neighbour in two columns, the page header indented by the card padding so the title, the card titles, the numbers and the plot share one…

name: Object header and a six-column grid
summary: The page header is the object itself: one card (88px, 14px padding) holding a 50x62 cover, the 18/600 name with 28px icon buttons beside it (open, copy, share), a 13px grey meta line (date, time, place) and outlined 36px actions on the right.

name: Per-period and running-total pairs
summary: Title at 24-32px with one sentence under it saying what the filters do, then one filter row of 36-38px controls (one filled or near-black, the rest borderless or text, a reset link last) and 16-24px to the KPIs.

name: Platform overview with a usage tray
summary: Sections stacked in one column about 48px apart, each with an 18/500 title on the left and a quiet action on the right ('View all', an outlined Refresh, a date-range button), and freshness in 14px grey after the title with a small status dot.

name: Power flow summary
summary: A strip under the title row that answers "where is the power going now?": four nodes in one row (Sun, House, Battery, Grid), each a 14px label over its live figure at 20-24px with the unit as a grey suffix (2.4 kW), the battery's charge under its figure (88%).

name: Report card with a legend table
summary: A report card (20/600 title, a kebab top right, a 32px select for the scope) whose body splits into a 390px left block and the chart.

name: Research lists and a long table
summary: Header: a 26/700 title over a 20px grey date, quiet pill buttons on the right; a 1px rule about 44px below, with the tabs just under it and the active tab marked by a 1px accent line as wide as its label lying on that rule.

name: Sell-out time strip
summary: One row per line that sold out, earliest first: the line and its shop on the left; a 2px grey track on a shared opening-to-closing axis with an ink dot at today's sell-out time and a hollow tick at the comparison day's (last Sunday), drawn with Charts.timeStrip(el, rows, { open, close,…

name: Settings in two columns
summary: A centred column of about 1152px.

name: Settings with usage on top
summary: Use this only when usage is the question of the view (a plan, billing or quota view), and show only numbers no section below repeats, at a size below the h1.

name: Tabbed object detail in a sheet
summary: Inside the sheet: a breadcrumb row at 16/600 (the parent in grey, the current page as the h1, a 24px grey type chip after it) with its actions on the right (a text button and an outlined 32px dropdown).

name: Table with tabs and a filter bar
summary: Title row: an 18-24px title on the left, at most an outlined secondary and the one primary (36px) on the right.

name: Team timeline with kind encoding
summary: People down the left on a 160-220px column, grouped under 12px team subheaders; days across with weekends one tone step darker, faint 1px day lines, and today as a 1px line in the one data hue with its date in ink in the header.

name: Workspace home with a greeting
summary: A centred column on a real 12-column grid (77px columns, 16px gutters, 1100px), about 72px from the top.
